description: Plan step R3a (graph node rules). Generalise the write engine: identity table, planning functions, the non-proposal operations, the property test. Permissions and audit: deep review. Depends on FEAT-003.
steps: Read rules design sec 2.5 (identity table), sec 7.4 (the write order, plan step incl. prune/expire), sec 9.2 (operations table), sec 15 R3 (engine cases) and the property-test paragraph of R2. Read src/rules/engine.ts, permissions.ts and tests/rules-engine.spec.ts.

Operations to build (each with a production caller in this or a later startable step): peak-mode-set (exists), rule-lift, rule-delete, rule-expire (harness only, with evidence, only when the deadline passed / until-condition holds / session released), signal-manual, signal-clear, signal-delete, ticket-open, ticket-update, ticket-handover, ticket-adopt, ticket-let-once, ticket-cancel, recovery-accept, recovery-dismiss, repo-adopt, repo-restore, repo-outside, repo-outside-cleared, notice-add, notice-delivered. NOT built (blocked on the approval path, list them in findings): propose, proposal-show/accept/reject/expire, rule-set, signal-define, detector-set/delete, repin, remove, signal-detected. rule-lift and rule-delete work on rules that arrive through the repository file (FEAT-003).

Write specs first: every cell of the 2.5 table for the built operations (human ok; llm forbidden; detector refused; harness only what the table lists); a request that claims another identity in its body is ignored (identity comes from the entry); revision check (stale_revision); a refused request writes no file; prune/expire changes carry cause and replay identically without the clock or the heartbeat directory (applyRecord reads no clock: replay under a frozen fake clock and an empty heartbeat directory gives the same state); closed tickets older than 24 h are not in the snapshot after the next write; tickets whose host heartbeat is gone become expired with expiredWhy host-gone.

Property test (5 fixed seeds, a hand-written generator, no new dev dependency, injected clock and a small rotation threshold): 200 writes per seed covering every built operation, at least one prune (clock +25 h, one host heartbeat file deleted), one journal rotation, two appended non-engine lines (one with a made-up snapshot, one without) followed by their recovery-accept / recovery-dismiss; afterwards (a) zero the snapshot, read once: replayed digest equals the pre-zero digest, skipped list empty, a new recovered record with reason snapshot-corrupt registers no row; (b) zero again: same digest, one more recovered record; (c) replay the whole journal directory from the empty state: digest equals (b)'s snapshot, base chain verifies. Failure prints the seed and the first sequence number that disagrees.

Implement permissions.ts (table), plan.ts (one planning function per operation, producing changes + the digest of the state after), engine.ts (apply dispatch; keep the existing lock, recovery and export order).
Docs in the same commit: docs/ORCHESTRATION.md section 16 operations table (built subset, stating the blocked ones).
Commit once: 'feat(rules): the write engine for the board operations that need no proposal (rules)' with gate results.

Script files in the repository are not written or deleted by this engine; rule-delete drops only the pin.

Design points interpreted rather than followed (flag to the reviewer / orchestrator):
1. Journal rotation (design 7.6) is built here. FEAT-003 did not build it and the property test (one rotation, replay of the whole directory) needs it. Order: copy journal -> journal-<last seq>.jsonl and fsync, then replace journal.jsonl by one rename with a base at nextSeq (state carried), then append the record (seq nextSeq+1), then snapshot. The reader links a file starting with a base at B to journal-<B-1>.jsonl only when the highest seq in that file is B-1 (my reading; it ignores stray copies and breaks cycles). If the replacing rename cannot be done after the retries the write fails with code io and nothing changed. Degenerate case not guarded: a rotateAtBytes smaller than the state rotates on every write.
2. Ticket gains optional clearedAt. The design's 30-minute rule for cleared tickets (7.4 step 5, 6.3) cannot be evaluated without the time of clearing and Ticket (7.2) has no field. ticket-update stamps it.
3. Request shapes are not in the design and were chosen: ticket-open flat fields (sessionId, agentLabel, host{pid,startedAt}, signature, tool, summary cut to 160 chars, rules, nested?, scriptRules?, pausedGoal?, pauseFailed?); ticket ids from q-1 (nextTicket set by the first open); notice ids n-<record seq>; signal-manual takes durationMs (1 ms to 7 days), the command parses '2h'; ticket-update fields and the transition table (deferred -> cleared|done|cancelled|expired, cleared -> done|cancelled|expired, closed states fixed, expired needs expiredWhy, the board stamps clearedAt/closedAt/resumedAt, resumed:true); ticket-let-once default now+10 min, until must be within 24 h; ticket-handover keeps the first handedFrom; ticket-adopt only for signature any:builtin:glm-peak-stop, lost (expired host-gone without resumedAt) goes back to deferred; recovery-* take labels.
4. rule-expire only confirms what state plus clock show: ttl due; until-condition true when every leaf is a clock or a switch (a signal with no detector); a condition naming glm-peak, a detector's signal or stage is never expired by the board (judging still treats it as ended at read time). A session rule needs request.released:true from the host (the state cannot show it) and never expires by itself. Later steps may extend this by letting the host pass facts; nothing has a caller yet.
5. Clean-up order for an open ticket: host-gone, then not-retried (cleared 30 min), then age (24 h). Entries the write itself touches are skipped. Closed tickets are pruned after more than 24 h.
6. Any write that changes the decided part rewrites rules.json and drops a pending repo.outside mark (the copy .rules.json.outside-* stays), as the slice's peak-mode-set did. A decided part that becomes empty removes rules.json (file 'removed'). If git is mid-operation that removal is deferred and the file then reads as an outside change, as for repo-restore.
7. repo-adopt and repo-restore call FEAT-003's adoptRepoLocked/restoreRepoLocked with their own records; they skip the clean-up and the rotation (the next write does both).
8. repo-outside and repo-outside-cleared are rows of the identity table (harness only) but not requestable (invalid); settleLocked writes them. Their identity cells are tested through refusalFor.
9. Ticket dedup (same session and signature, 20 open per session, root-chain reuse) is NOT in the engine; FEAT-007's tickets.ts must dedupe before ticket-open.
10. The plan decides host liveness from <runtimeDir>/hosts/<pid>-<startedAt>.json, reading only its at (fresh = 45 s). FEAT-007 must write that file (before ticket-open) or the next write expires the ticket as host-gone. HostHeartbeat's full shape and liveHeartbeats are FEAT-005/007's.
11. The row (src/rules/index.ts) still only calls peak-mode-set and its failureText says 高峰模式没有改 for any error; FEAT-006 should generalize it when it adds the other commands.
12. replayJournals is exported for the design's check (c) and is called by tests only; production reads use journalChain directly.
13. A refused request still lets the settle that precedes every write persist recovery or an outside-file record first (as before); that is the only file a refused request can write.
